thread.label: Genesis 39:1-12
thread.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.

classes.title: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 9:9
precepts.why:
“the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” And “Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured”: he had a very good reputation, and people looked at him as a man of integrity and good character.

Then his master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” He refused: his master had committed all that he had to his hand, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. That is where integrity comes from: making the right decision when nobody is watching.

Ecclesiasticus 9:9 gives the same wisdom as a command: “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” Do not sit with another man’s wife at all. Do not play with it. Do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife, because your heart will incline to her, and both of you will destroy everything.

Joseph lived that. When “there was none of the men of the house there within,” she caught him by his garment, “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” He knew it was wickedness that would destroy his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for, and that he would not only be sinning against her but against the Lord. He fled rather than sit with it, even though he went to prison when she lied on him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 4:27
precepts.why:
When Moses died, the mantle passed to Joshua, and the people answered him: “According as we hearkened unto Moses in all things, so will we hearken unto thee: only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” They hearkened to Moses because they believed he was the man of the Lord. Moses led the people with integrity and character, even while judging Israel in the wilderness, and he kept that integrity all the way.

Yet there are negroes online, some elders from other camps, certain unsavory Black Hebrew Israelite camps, saying that Moses left the truth, that he was off and didn't have the spirit. What are you talking about? It says right there in verse 17: “only the Lord thy God be with thee, as he was with Moses.” The Lord was with Moses. Shame on you for not reading the scriptures, and shame on the men that follow you.

Because Sirach says, “Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty.” Camps like that have made themselves students and underlings to a negro that's just as dumb as they are.

Israel followed Joshua because they had seen Moses' character in him while he ministered under Moses. The company you keep matters. Joshua was under Moses, and Caleb did the same thing, and they learned integrity and good character by being under a man the Lord was with. Put yourself under a foolish man, and you learn his folly instead.

precepts.label: Galatians 6:1-2
precepts.why:
Job's three friends heard of all the evil that came upon him, came every one from his own place “to mourn with him and to comfort him”, and “sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.” Now you see the type of men you are around. That is true friendship, and Galatians shows what it is supposed to do.

“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” When a brother falls, you have to build and restore this man back to life. Speak life into that brother to get him back on track, in meekness, remembering you could be tempted too.

“Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” If we were in that same situation, we would want our brothers to come and get us out of it.

Job held fast his integrity when he lost his kids, lost everything he had, and had boils all over his body. Satan came in through his wife, “curse God, and die”, but Job answered, “shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” A man going through that needs brothers who will sit with him, carry his burden with him and restore him, not tear him down.

precepts.label: Romans 6:1
precepts.why:
The question put to the class: you're alone online late at night, temptation hits, and nobody from the congregation would know. What shows integrity? A, entertain the temptation privately. B, watch a little and justify it later. C, cut it off immediately and fight temptation. D, convince yourself grace covers everything. Answer D is a scary mindset to have, and Paul already answered it: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?”

Shall we continue in sin that grace may cover everything? That is a terrible mindset, and it is the mindset of Christianity: I found grace, grace covers me, I can do what I want when I want. All I have to do is believe in Jesus; I ain't got to do nothing he says, just believe he's my Lord and savior. Christianity is evil.

The answer is C. The questions are easy and the answers are easy; the problem is when it comes to fruition in real time. You are fighting your war against yourself: you don't want to push play, but you want to push play, and nobody is there to tell you a damn thing. That is when C gets blurred out.

The real battlefield is private. A lot of people fall spiritually in secret long before they fall publicly. The representative shows up at the Sabbath; the real you shows up at home, alone, with your family, and your wife knows exactly who you are. You can't salute so hard you're over righteous and then go home and verbally, financially or physically abuse your wife. And sisters, you can't bow 90 degrees at the door and then go home, cuss your husband out, and keep a filthy house. That is lacking integrity and poor character.

That is Proverbs 11:3: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.” Grace is not a cover for sin; integrity is acting on what you know, even when nobody is watching.

precepts.label: Proverbs 17:10
precepts.why:
“He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul”. He doesn't want to hear it; he doesn't want to be corrected; he's always right, but wrong as hell. That isn't hurting somebody else; you are destroying your own soul, because you can't be corrected, which means you can't grow. This is why: “A reproof entereth more into a wise man than an hundred stripes into a fool.”

As a foolish person, you cannot allow wisdom to enter in. You're sitting around the men, you're in the school with all these men, you see everybody growing around you, and for some reason you know everything, but the wisdom can't take hold and exalt you the way it exalts all the rest who take hold of it. You're fighting against it.

That is why some have been in the truth 10 or 15 years and are still a soldier. How long you been with us? 10 years. What's your rank? Officer of 10, sir. Why? I don't know, sir. You know. You know everything else but that. You can't say you've been held back. Ten years and you're only able to deal with ten men: that is a problem.

That is when it is time to take stock in yourself, and a lot of people don't want to do that, because they don't want the integrity that comes with the Bible. The one who hears reproof gets understanding; the fool takes a hundred stripes and learns nothing.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:6
precepts.why:
Judas is the character we are not to have. “This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag.” He walked with Christ and saw many miracles, and still betrayed the savior and everybody around him. Money was his root and his god: greed. That is how they infiltrate organizations: they come in and offer money, and a people lacking integrity gives up the organization and lets money dictate and control the movement. That ain't happening here.

Israel is to give the nations the opposite: “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” Keeping the law is our wisdom, and it is seen.

When your coworkers wonder why this brother doesn't murmur with them and never works the Sabbath, that is the nations seeing the statutes kept. The other nations are expecting you to be that greedy individual that lacks integrity, a Judas who can be bought. We give them this right here: character and integrity, the hidden strength behind wisdom.

precepts.label: Tobit 6:10-17
precepts.why:
“But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin”. The thoughts warring against your mind are Satan, and one of the ways he brings you into the captivity of bitterness is over who is talking to whom. Brothers stop talking to a brother because of a sister. Two sisters were cool, both liked the same brother, and now they have stopped talking to each other. That is bitterness, and that is fake.

Tobit shows how God brings people together. The angel told Tobias, “to day we shall lodge with Raguel, who is thy cousin; he also hath one only daughter, named Sara; I will speak for her, that she may be given thee for a wife. For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred.” And he told him, when he came into the marriage chamber and made the smoke, “the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more”, and they should rise up both of them and pray to God.

Then: “fear not, for she is appointed unto thee from the beginning”. From ever since the beginning, that was his wife. The Most High does bring people together. If that brother is for you, he is for you. Whoever is for you is for you.

So do not develop bitterness and hatred toward each other over who is talking to whom. Be happy for the brother; be happy for the sister. You brothers cannot stop talking to each other because of a woman, and brothers who roll like that need to repent. That bitterness is going to change you, and it is just a matter of time before you leave the body. “With the mind I myself serve the law of God”: when those evil thoughts about your brother or sister come, shake them off.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 11:7
precepts.why:
We were warned: “in the last days perilous times shall come”, and among the men of those days are “false accusers.” Sirach gives the law against it: “Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.”

You cannot accuse, you cannot blame, until you have seen all that needs to be seen concerning a matter. How many people run their mouth without understanding, without knowing? How many gossip without the full understanding of what is going on, yet have so many opinions and thoughts on how this should be, on what so-and-so is doing and shouldn’t be doing? You look foolish when you do this without understanding what is going on.

If your opinion lacks understanding, if it lacks the pertinent information needed to explain what is going on, but you still feel it necessary to give it, something is wrong with you. You have been put in many situations that showed you that you jumped the gun, that you didn’t know what was going on. Yet and still you feel your opinion matters. It doesn’t. Understand first, and then rebuke.

That goes with the pride Paul names. The prideful spirit won’t allow you to take any correction or accept what is being said; it has you thinking it is everybody but you. And it goes with the “despisers of those that are good”: people who hate that you are doing what you are supposed to do, that you are above them in rank and active in the body. Every time you turn around they have a suggestion nobody asked for, and they don’t say it to you; they tell everybody underneath you, so all your peers know how they feel. You never know them for exhorting anybody, only for bringing problems about everything they see.

The law says “Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people.” The talebearer with the tea, who somehow knows before leadership knows, is the fuel that keeps reputations scarred and people at odds. And when you tell a story as if you know what is going on, without the whole story, and it is not true, that is a lie: “he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.” That is why you must examine the truth before you blame.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 18:27
precepts.why:
Sirach says “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing, whatever situation or inconvenience he is in. Our integrity, our moral character, is directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

Chapter 18 shows that fear at work: “A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step. Every step you are asking, is this the right move to make? Is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“And in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself. He has the fear of God in him and he is walking in his integrity. “But a fool will not observe time.”

The same goes for moments of correction. If you are dealing with the leadership and you cannot take the correction, if you are unable to digest it, understand it, take it and receive it, that is a sign of where your faith and your belief are.

So we have to make sure we are walking in the fear of the Lord. That fear is “the root of wisdom”, and where it is present it drives away sin and “turneth away wrath.”
